problem_statement: The paper frames the task as using variational quantum classifiers to model relationships in financial market data, specifically the evolution of the BET index relative to other major stock indices. It treats this as a classification problem of predicting whether BET will increase or decrease from the available index information.
problem_statement_quotes: The effectiveness of the method is evaluated using real financial data, modeling the evolution of the BET index in relation t0 well-known indices from neighboring Central and Eastern European countries, as well as from Western Europe and the United States.

classical_baseline: The paper compares its noisy variational quantum classifier against a baseline variational quantum classifier without the noise mechanism, and also against standard classical machine-learning classifiers such as logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, k-nearest neighbors, and support vector machines.
classical_baseline_quotes: We compare our method with both the baseline quantum classifier used and a suite of classical machine learning techniques (lo- gistic regression, decision trees, random forests, k-nearest neighbors, and support vector machines)

classical_difficulty: The paper says the task is challenging for classical approaches in the sense that the data are difficult and the classification problem is hard, but it does not give a formal complexity result. It emphasizes that the financial data involve complex, nonlinear dependencies and that the classical methods show overfitting and only moderate test accuracy on the benchmark.
